advice: Propose a fused A-panel pack-and-compute path for n=512. In gemm, allocate a 64 KiB buffer for a 32-row A panel. For each row band r=0,32,…,480, use ZA transpose operations on small FP32 tiles from A[(r+i)*512+k] and write the transposed values to pack[k*32+i]. Then call sera_libxsmm_panel32 sixteen times, once per band, with parameters[4]=B, parameters[10]=A+r*512, parameters[16]=C+r*512 as specified. This tests whether doing the transpose while filling the panel is useful; the helper still performs its own internal packing, so count that repeated work, every buffer write, all sixteen calls, and SME transitions in the timed call. This differs from leaving the helper unused and from a standalone full-A transpose. Keep the original LIBXSMM full512 path available as fallback if allocation fails, and keep all other n values on the existing fallback. The fused transpose cannot feed the helper as described: its fixed ABI reads A+r*512 directly and packs internally, so the new panel buffer would be unused by the helper. Do not submit this exact design as a runnable performance candidate unless the call/data-layout plan is revised so the helper actually consumes the packed panel; with the supplied helper, no useful fused transpose experiment is established.
risks: The proposed helper arguments leave no slot for the new packed panel, and its generated body performs its own packing. Adding a transpose would therefore add work without changing the helper's inputs. Any revised design must preserve the row-major product, FP32 arithmetic, full general-size behavior and timed allocation/packing, then pass full GEMM correctness for n=512 and general sizes/tails, n<=0, the 0.002 tolerance, and paired unchanged controls on the block's fixed power mode. No performance result or speedup is established by the supplied evidence.
